name: tarans

attributes.attribute: spirits of unbaptized infants in wild places
blend the Otherworld with the Christian Limbo

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tarans are spirits in Scottish folklore. They are the souls of babies who died before baptism. People saw them in wild and lonely places. The spirits wept because they could not reach heaven. The belief joins the Celtic picture of the other world with the Christian idea of Limbo. In that teaching, unbaptized infants must wait forever even though they did no wrong.

okr.objective: Record the tarans as the spirits of unbaptized unborn children.
key_results: Names the tarans as spirits of the unbaptized dead
Places them in wild and lonely places
Notes the belief joins the Otherworld and the Christian Limbo
